knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to score prospects against written criteria, including service area and repeat need. A group of clients with several treatments inside the service area that you already see meets those criteria. A one-off job far outside the area fails the service-area test, and a website does not show a repeat need.

The lesson says a public notice does not by itself permit contact, and that contact must use published business details and the electronic message and do-not-call rules. Of the options, only the business-route approach avoids a rule the lesson states. Using residents' private details or entering the common area are both ruled out.
The lesson says to confirm the Spam Act 2003 requirements in current ACMA guidance before sending a commercial email. Subject-line style and social media likes are not the rule.

practicalCriteria: Learner scores a supplied list of ten prospects against the written criteria and gives each a strong, possible or not-a-fit rating with a stated reason.
Learner writes a first message that states how the business was identified, includes one verifiable observation and offers one small next step that is easy to decline.
Learner records a stop request in the list and shows that the contact is removed from the next follow-up schedule.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Scored prospect list with a reason for each rating
First message draft checked against the electronic message rules
Stop-request record with the date actioned
stopWorkCriteria: Learner uses private information about an individual to make contact
Learner sends an email or text to a prospect without checking the electronic message rules
Learner offers a licensed or authorised service without holding the licence for it
